full_judgment:
5. Mr. Iqbal Kalam Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that the predecessor of the plaintiffs namely Md. Abdur Rob was the owner and possessor of the disputed land who filed the suit on 15-4-2012 for cancellation of two deeds of gift in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Noakhali, claiming the impugned two deeds of gift are fraudulent, .forged, without consideration, illegal, ineffective. Subsequently, the suit was transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Begumganj, Noakhali and renumbered as Title Suit No. 542 of 2016. He further submits that after corona pandemic, in the year 2021, the newly engaged lawyer found that the plaint of the suit should have been filed with a prayer for declaration instead of cancellation that the plaintiffs have title and the two deeds of gift are not binding upon the plaintiffs. He also submits that the newly engaged learned Advocate for the plaintiffs having known it, filed the amendment petition on 4-1-2021 under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, which was illegally rejected on 11-11-2021 and later, another amendment petition was filed on 26-7-2022 under Order VI, rule 17 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to reconsider the rejection order and allow the amendment petition, but the Trial Court illegally rejected the same vide order dated 26-7-2022 with a wrong finding that the plaintiffs are stopped to the amendment petition and the prayer is barred by limitation. He further submits that the revisional Court failed to consider the legal aspects that proposed amendment would not change the nature and character of the suit and it is necessary for final adjudication and determination of the real question in controversy between the parties and, as such, both the courts below committed errors of law in their decisions occasioning failure of justice for which he prays for setting aside the impugned judgment and order passed in the Civil Revision No. 29 of 2022. In support of his contention, he relied upon the decisions passed in the cases of Jarina Khatun and others vs Pizlin Chandra Das and others reported in Vol. V 1985 BLD (AD) 253 : 37 DLR (AD).67, Alimuddin and others vs Abdul Kabir and others reported in 58 DLR 240, Abul Hasnat vs Md. Alauddin reported in 63 DLR 141 and Managing Committee NMC Model High School and others vs Ohaidur Rahman Chowdhury and others reported in 31 DLR (AD) 131. 

 8. Thereafter, Mr. Hasan submits that the claim of the plaintiffs, for amending the plaint for declaration of their title and the two deeds of gift are not binding upon them, is also barred by limitation. 

 22. The learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 submits that the claim of the plaintiff-petitioners is barred by the law of limitation since the amendment petition has been filed after the statutory period of 06 (six) years for a decree of declaration from the date of accrual of case of action on 27-3-2012, but the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that if the amendment petition is allowed then it will not be barred by law of limitation. In suppoft of his submission, he referred the decision passed in the case of farina Khatun and others vs Pulin Chandra Das and others reported in Vol V, 1985 BLD (AD) 253 : 37 DLR (AD) 67 according to which in case of amendment petition, the court shall consider two questions firstly, whether the claim to be included was barred by the law of limitation on the date of institution of the suit. Secondly, whether the claim is barred by limitation on the date of the prayer for amendment. On the first, the prayer for amendment cannot be allowed as it was barred on the date of filing the suit. On the second, however, the prayer could be allowed subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions. 

 23. In the light of the decisions passed in the case reported in Vol V, 1985 BLD (AD) 253 : 37 DLR (AD) 67 the proposed amendment is not barred by the law of limitation. In this regard I find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioners.
